CSB & Weather Data Analysis¶

This notebook merges the processed Crop Sequence Boundaries (CSB) acreage data with aggregated weather data to explore relationships between climate variables and planting decisions.

3. Process & Aggregate Weather Data¶

Goal: Create Annual-County level weather metrics (e.g., Total Precip during Growing Season)¶

In [56]:
if 'weather_df' in locals():
    # Convert dates
    weather_df['start_date'] = pd.to_datetime(weather_df['start_date'])
    weather_df['Year'] = weather_df['start_date'].dt.year
    weather_df['Month'] = weather_df['start_date'].dt.month
    
    # Filter for Growing Season (April - October)
    # Adjust months as needed for specific crops
    growing_season = weather_df[weather_df['Month'].between(4, 10)]
    
    # Aggregate
    weather_annual = growing_season.groupby(['county_name', 'Year']).agg({
        'totr': 'sum',       # Total Rainfall
        'avgt': 'mean',      # Average Temperature
        'gdd_b10': 'sum',    # Growing Degree Days (Base 10C approx Base 50F)
        'mint': 'min',       # Minimum Temperature recorded
        'maxt': 'max'        # Maximum Temperature recorded
    }).reset_index()
    
    # Rename columns for merging
    weather_annual.rename(columns={
        'county_name': 'CNTY',
        'totr': 'Total_Precip_AprOct',
        'avgt': 'Avg_Temp_AprOct',
        'gdd_b10': 'GDD_AprOct',
        'mint': 'Min_Temp_AprOct',
        'maxt': 'Max_Temp_AprOct'
    }, inplace=True)
    
    print("Weather Aggregation Complete.")
    display(weather_annual.head())

# 3.1 Feature Engineering: Seasonal Weather Metrics & Anomalies

if 'weather_df' in locals():
    # Define seasons
    planting_season = weather_df[weather_df['Month'].between(4, 5)]
    growing_season = weather_df[weather_df['Month'].between(6, 8)]
    harvest_season = weather_df[weather_df['Month'].between(9, 10)]
    
    # Helper function to aggregate
    def aggregate_season(df, prefix):
        agg = df.groupby(['county_name', 'Year']).agg({
            'totr': 'sum',
            'avgt': 'mean',
            'gdd_b10': 'sum',
            'maxt': lambda x: (x > 32.2).sum() # Count days > 90F (32.2C)
        }).reset_index()
        agg.rename(columns={
            'totr': f'{prefix}_Precip',
            'avgt': f'{prefix}_AvgTemp',
            'gdd_b10': f'{prefix}_GDD',
            'maxt': f'{prefix}_HeatDays'
        }, inplace=True)
        return agg

    # Aggregate by season
    plant_agg = aggregate_season(planting_season, 'Planting')
    grow_agg = aggregate_season(growing_season, 'Growing')
    harv_agg = aggregate_season(harvest_season, 'Harvest')
    
    # Merge all seasonal data
    seasonal_weather = pd.merge(plant_agg, grow_agg, on=['county_name', 'Year'], how='outer')
    seasonal_weather = pd.merge(seasonal_weather, harv_agg, on=['county_name', 'Year'], how='outer')
    
    # Rename for consistency
    seasonal_weather.rename(columns={'county_name': 'CNTY'}, inplace=True)
    
    # Calculate Anomalies (Deviation from 5-year rolling average)
    # We need to sort by Year to calculate rolling stats
    seasonal_weather.sort_values(['CNTY', 'Year'], inplace=True)
    
    metrics = ['Planting_Precip', 'Growing_GDD', 'Growing_Precip']
    for metric in metrics:
        # Calculate 5-year rolling mean (closed window, min_periods=1)
        seasonal_weather[f'{metric}_5y_Avg'] = seasonal_weather.groupby('CNTY')[metric].transform(
            lambda x: x.rolling(window=5, min_periods=1).mean().shift(1) # Shift to use PAST 5 years
        )
        # Calculate Deviation
        seasonal_weather[f'{metric}_Anomaly'] = seasonal_weather[metric] - seasonal_weather[f'{metric}_5y_Avg']
    
    print("Seasonal Weather & Anomalies Created.")
    display(seasonal_weather.head())

3.2 Distribution Analysis of Weather Variables¶

In this section, we examine the distribution of key weather variables:

  • Planting_Precip: Total precipitation during planting season (April-May).
  • Growing_GDD: Accumulated Growing Degree Days during the growing season (June-August).

We compare the original distributions with log-transformed versions to address potential skewness in the data. Understanding these distributions is crucial for statistical modeling assumptions.

In [58]:
# 3.2 Distribution Analysis: Weather Variables
# Analyzing the distribution of key weather variables (Original vs Log Transformed)

if 'seasonal_weather' in locals():
    # Key variables to analyze
    vars_to_analyze = ['Planting_Precip', 'Growing_GDD']
    
    # 1. Summary of Data Dimensions
    print(f"Data Dimensions: {seasonal_weather.shape}")
    print(f"Unique Counties: {seasonal_weather['CNTY'].nunique()}")
    if 'Year' in seasonal_weather.columns:
        years = seasonal_weather['Year'].unique()
        print(f"Years Covered: {min(years)} - {max(years)}")
    
    # 2. Descriptive Statistics
    print("\n--- Summary Statistics (Original Data) ---")
    display(seasonal_weather[vars_to_analyze].describe())
    
    # 3. Visualizing Distributions (Original vs Log Transformed)
    # Histograms
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(vars_to_analyze), 2, figsize=(15, 6 * len(vars_to_analyze)))
    
    for i, var in enumerate(vars_to_analyze):
        # Prepare Data
        data = seasonal_weather[var].dropna()
        log_data = np.log1p(data)
        
        # Row i, Col 0: Original Data (Histogram + KDE)
        sns.histplot(data, kde=True, ax=axes[i, 0], color='skyblue')
        axes[i, 0].set_title(f'Original Distribution: {var}')
        axes[i, 0].set_xlabel(var)
        
        # Row i, Col 1: Log Transformed Data (Histogram + KDE)
        sns.histplot(log_data, kde=True, ax=axes[i, 1], color='salmon')
        axes[i, 1].set_title(f'Log Transformed Distribution: {var}')
        axes[i, 1].set_xlabel(f'Log({var})')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    # Box Plots
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(vars_to_analyze), 2, figsize=(15, 6 * len(vars_to_analyze)))
        
    for i, var in enumerate(vars_to_analyze):
        data = seasonal_weather[var].dropna()
        log_data = np.log1p(data)
        
        # Row i, Col 0: Original Box Plot
        sns.boxplot(x=data, ax=axes[i, 0], color='skyblue')
        axes[i, 0].set_title(f'Original Box Plot: {var}')
        axes[i, 0].set_xlabel(var)
        
        # Row i, Col 1: Log Transformed Box Plot
        sns.boxplot(x=log_data, ax=axes[i, 1], color='salmon')
        axes[i, 1].set_title(f'Log Transformed Box Plot: {var}')
        axes[i, 1].set_xlabel(f'Log({var})')
        
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# 4. Merge Datasets (Enhanced)

if 'csb_df' in locals() and 'seasonal_weather' in locals():
    # Merge CSB with Seasonal Weather
    merged_df = pd.merge(csb_df, seasonal_weather, on=['CNTY', 'Year'], how='inner')
    
    # 4.1 Lagged Variables (Crop Rotation)
    # We want to know the acreage of the SAME crop in the PREVIOUS year
    merged_df.sort_values(['CNTY', 'Crop_Name', 'Year'], inplace=True)
    merged_df['Acres_Lag1'] = merged_df.groupby(['CNTY', 'Crop_Name'])['CSBACRES'].shift(1)
    
    # 4.2 Soil Data (Placeholder - assuming static soil file exists or creating dummy)

    if os.path.exists(soil_path):
        soil_df = pd.read_csv(soil_path)
        merged_df = pd.merge(merged_df, soil_df, on='CNTY', how='left')
    else:

if 'merged_df' in locals():
    # Aggregate to State Level
    state_annual = merged_df.groupby(['Year', 'Crop_Name']).agg({
        'CSBACRES': 'sum',
        'Planting_Precip': 'mean', # Average of county averages
        'Growing_GDD': 'mean'
    }).reset_index()
    
    # --- 6.1 All Major Crops (Raw Scale) ---

    all_crops = ['Corn', 'Soybeans', 'Alfalfa', 'Winter Wheat']
    
    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 7))
    
    # Plot Acreage
    colors = ['tab:blue', 'tab:orange', 'tab:green', 'tab:red']

        crop_data = state_annual[state_annual['Crop_Name'] == crop]
        ax1.plot(crop_data['Year'], crop_data['CSBACRES'], marker='o', label=f'{crop} Acres', color=colors[i])
    
    ax1.set_ylabel('Total Acres', color='black')
    ax1.set_xlabel('Year')
    ax1.legend(loc='upper left')
    ax1.grid(True)
    
    # Plot Weather (Secondary Axis)
    ax2 = ax1.twinx()

    ax2.set_ylabel('Avg Precip (inches)', color='gray')
    ax2.legend(loc='upper right')

Interpretation of Statewide Trends¶

The plots above visualize the relationship between total annual planting acreage and average spring precipitation (April-May) across New York State.

1. Mismatched Y-Axis Scales: In the original separate plots, the Y-axis ranges were different because Corn (~1,000,000 acres) and Soybeans (~300,000 acres) are planted on a much larger scale than Winter Wheat (~30,000 acres) or Alfalfa. When plotted separately, matplotlib automatically scales the axis to fit the data range of that specific subset. When combined into a single linear plot, the smaller crops (Wheat) appear as flat lines at the bottom because their variance is tiny compared to the scale required for Corn.

2. Log-Transformed Plot: The Log-Scale plot solves this visualization issue. By compressing the Y-axis, we can clearly see the relative trends (percentage changes) for all crops simultaneously. For example, a 10% drop in Wheat acreage is now visible alongside a 10% drop in Corn acreage, even though the absolute acreages differ by an order of magnitude.

3. Observations:

  • Corn: Shows a generally stable or slightly increasing trend over the years. Notice specific years where acreage drops (e.g., if visible in 2011, 2019, etc.), which often corresponds to spikes in planting season precipitation. Heavy spring rain delays planting, sometimes forcing farmers to abandon acres or switch to shorter-season crops.
  • Soybeans: Often acts as a substitute for corn. In years where planting is delayed (high precip), soybean acreage might hold steady or increase as it has a shorter growing window.
  • Alfalfa: Being a perennial crop (planted once every few years), its annual acreage fluctuation is less sensitive to immediate spring weather compared to annual row crops. However, extreme wetness can damage stands (winter kill or root rot), influencing replanting decisions.
  • Winter Wheat: Planted in the fall (previous year). Its harvested acreage is influenced by fall weather conditions (planting window) and winter survival rates, rather than just the spring weather shown here. However, wet springs can affect the harvest quality or timing.

7. Panel Data Modeling (Fixed Effects)¶

We estimate the following Fixed Effects model to control for unobserved county-specific characteristics (like soil quality or topography) and year-specific shocks (like prices or policy).

Model Equation¶

$$ Acres_{it} = \alpha + \beta_1 Acres_{i,t-1} + \beta_2 Weather_{it} + \mu_i + \lambda_t + \epsilon_{it} $$

Where:

  • $Acres_{it}$: Planted acreage in county $i$ at year $t$.
  • $Acres_{i,t-1}$: Lagged acreage (Crop Rotation effect).
  • $Weather_{it}$: Vector of weather variables (Precip, GDD, etc.).
  • $\mu_i$: County Fixed Effects (Time-invariant).
  • $\lambda_t$: Year Fixed Effects (Time-variant shocks).
  • $\epsilon_{it}$: Error term.

# 7.1 Install linearmodels if not present
# !pip install linearmodels

from linearmodels.panel import PanelOLS
import statsmodels.api as sm

if 'merged_df' in locals():
    # Prepare Data for Panel Model
    # We need a MultiIndex of (Entity, Time) -> (CNTY, Year)
    panel_data = merged_df.copy()
    
    # Filter for a specific crop (e.g., Corn) for the model
    # Modeling all crops together might be noisy unless we use Seemingly Unrelated Regressions (SUR)
    target_crop = 'Corn'
    model_df = panel_data[panel_data['Crop_Name'] == target_crop].copy()
    
    # Set Index
    model_df = model_df.set_index(['CNTY', 'Year'])
    
    # Define Predictors (X) and Target (y)
    # Include Lagged Acres and Weather Metrics
    predictors = [
        'Acres_Lag1', 
        'Planting_Precip', 
        'Growing_GDD', 
        'Growing_Precip', 
        'Harvest_Precip'
    ]
    
    # Drop rows with NaN (due to lagging or missing weather)
    model_data = model_df[predictors + ['CSBACRES']].dropna()
    
    # Define X and y
    y = model_data['CSBACRES']
    X = model_data[predictors]
    
    # Add Constant
    X = sm.add_constant(X)
    
    print(f"--- Panel Model for {target_crop} ---")
    
    # 1. Fixed Effects Model (Entity Effects Only)
    # entity_effects=True adds County Fixed Effects
    mod_fe = PanelOLS(y, X, entity_effects=True)
    res_fe = mod_fe.fit(cov_type='clustered', cluster_entity=True)
    print(res_fe)
    
    # 2. Two-Way Fixed Effects Model (Entity + Time Effects)
    # time_effects=True adds Year Fixed Effects
    print(f"\n--- Two-Way Fixed Effects Model for {target_crop} ---")
    mod_twfe = PanelOLS(y, X, entity_effects=True, time_effects=True)
    res_twfe = mod_twfe.fit(cov_type='clustered', cluster_entity=True)
    print(res_twfe)
